title: I packaged my whole “concept art → Blender → Godot → shipped build” workflow as a Claude Code skill. The goal is AI-made games that aren’t slop
author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
selftext:
I’ve been making small 3D games almost entirely with Claude Code. The latest is **Alchemists of Prague**, an action RPG in the spirit of Gothic 1–2, set in medieval Prague around 1400. I wanted something you can actually play for a while, not a pile of mismatched store assets with an LLM wrapper on top. So I turned the whole process into a reusable skill:

    /plugin marketplace add msveshnikov/alchemists-of-prague
    /plugin install game-pipeline@alchemists-of-prague

Repo (game + skill): [https://github.com/msveshnikov/alchemists-of-prague](https://github.com/msveshnikov/alchemists-of-prague)

**How the pipeline works**

1. **Design doc + style block.** One paragraph describing the art style (era, palette, light, camera) goes at the start of every image prompt, so all the art matches.
2. **Concept art from ChatGPT**, ordered through the Claude desktop app’s built-in browser with my normal account. No API keys. Claude types the prompts, downloads the images, and can attach a reference image (with a small workaround, which is in the skill). Every location gets day, night and “empty” versions. There are also character sheets and UI screens.
3. **Five task files, each run autonomously:** Claude doesn’t ask questions. It logs every decision in [`decisions.md`](http://decisions.md), every failure in [`issues.md`](http://issues.md), and writes a report at the end.
   * task1: environment and props
   * task2: characters, rigs, animations
   * task3: empty levels, markers, day/night lighting
   * task4: population and effects
   * task5: the game in Godot
4. **Everything 3D is generated by Python running headless in Blender:** about 10k lines building 101 glTF assets. That covers models, numpy-painted textures, rigs, skin weights, procedural animations (including a foot-planted IK gait) and level layouts. No 3D generators, nothing hand-modelled. Any asset rebuilds with one command.
5. **Godot 4 builds the level at runtime from JSON** that Blender writes, so a rebuilt level shows up in the game without anyone editing scenes. The UI is code too (about 6.9k lines of GDScript in total).
6. **Vertical slice first:** all five tasks for one location, play it, fix the task files, then do a second run for the other districts and stitch them into one world.
7. **Every task ends with shipping:** commit, export Windows + Web + Android, upload, open the live page and check it.

**Why I think it’s less sloppy than usual**

* **One style, enforced.** The style block goes into every prompt, plus shared texture palettes and strict naming conventions (`INT_door_*`, `MARK_*`, `LIGHT_*`).
* **The agent has to look at its own output:** preview renders, contact sheets, in-game screenshot tours, compared against the concept art.
* **An** `--autotest` **mode plays the game by itself** (moving, fighting, trading, entering a house, throwing an enemy out of a window, night, save/load, death) and writes screenshots and a log.
* **When something looks primitive, we iterate with reference art.** Example: the in-game map used to be a raw top-down render. Claude gave ChatGPT a crop of the real layout, had it write a better prompt, then generate a parchment map. Then it aligned the painting back to the layout with OpenCV, so the player arrow sits exactly where you stand.

**Honest limits:** 6–10 FPS on Intel integrated graphics (much better on a real GPU or in the browser build), simple geometric faces, no quests yet, a debug-signed APK. It’s a solid prototype, not a finished product.

The skill includes the prompt templates, the task1–5 templates, the Blender and Godot conventions, the ChatGPT-in-browser steps, the alignment script and the shipping checklist. Feedback welcome, especially from anyone who tries it on a completely different genre.

comments.author: Just-Routine967
comments.body: Is there anything extra it's doing to ensure accurate visual comparisons? Claude's attention to detail there is pretty lacking unless you get it to use bright debug colouring and breaking down screenshots into zoomed chunks, just telling it to compare them will miss so much.

replies.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
replies.body: Opus 5.5 on high or xhigh effort usually is good with details. Only Fable 5.2 is better

replies.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
replies.body: I used it mostly for humanoid main characters
